rule.message: A Calendar is inefficient in memory usage.
rule.description: Problem: A Calendar is a heavyweight object and expensive to create. Solution: Use java.time.LocalDateTime or java.time.ZonedDateTime instead. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidImplicitlyRecompilingRegex
rule.message: String regex method, Pattern.matches or FileSystem.getPathMatcher is used. Implicitly compiles a regex pattern, can be expensive.
rule.description: A regular expression is compiled implicitly on every invocation. Problem: this can be expensive, depending on the length of the regular expression. rule.name: AvoidInMemoryStreamingDefaultConstructor
rule.message: The default capacity or smaller is used for ByteArrayOutputStream or StringWriter, it usually needs expensive expansions.
rule.description: The default constructor of ByteArrayOutputStream creates a 32-byte initial capacity and for StringWriter 16 chars. Problem: Such a small buffer as capacity usually needs several expensive expansions. Solution: Pre-size the ByteArrayOutputStream or StringWriter with an initial capacity such that an expansion is not needed in most cases, typically much larger than 32, for instance, 4096. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidLoadingAllFromFile
rule.message: Files.readAll methods and similar APIs load all bytes into memory: a risk of memory problems.
rule.description: Problem: APIs like Files.readAllBytes, Files.readAllLines, Files.readString, InputStream.readAllBytes, IOUtils.toByteArray, ByteArrayOutputStream.toByteArray load entire content into heap memory. This risks OutOfMemoryError, long GC pauses, and slow responses when processing large files. Solution: Use streaming APIs end-to-end, do not buffer whole files in memory. Note: Not a problem for small files. Use @SuppressWarnings("PMD.AvoidLoadingAllFromFile") then. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidRecompilingXPathExpression
rule.message: XPathExpression is created and compiled every time. Beware it is thread-unsafe.
rule.description: XPathExpression is created and compiled on every method call, compiled possibly implicitly by XPath::evaluate. Caching it in a ThreadLocal may be a solution. (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: BufferFileStreaming
rule.message: FileInputStream or FileOutputStream used without buffering. Wrap with BufferedInputStream or BufferedOutputStream.
rule.description: Problem: With FileInputStream and FileOutputStream, file access is not buffered. The stream is read-from/written-to file byte by byte, where each operating system call has its overhead, which makes it slow. Solution: Use buffering to read/write a chunk of bytes at once with much lower overhead. Use BufferedOutput/InputStream which has a buffer size of 8 kB by default to write at once. Make sure to close it after use. (jpinpoint-rules)

fun bad(name: String): ByteArray = FileInputStream(name).use { it.readBytes() } // bad
fun good(name: String): ByteArray = BufferedInputStream(FileInputStream(name)).use { it.readBytes() } // ok

rule.name: AvoidCommonPoolForFutureAsync
rule.message: Avoid using the common thread pool for future.supplyAsync, use a separate pool.
rule.description: Problem: CompletableFuture.supplyAsync is typically used for remote calls. By default, it uses the common pool. Solution: A separate, properly sized, pool of threads (an Executor) should be used for the async calls. (jpinpoint-rules) (jpinpoint-rules)

rule.name: AvoidParallelFlux
rule.message: Avoid Flux.parallel for iterable sources: it divides data on CPU-count rails which is usually slower for non-CPU-intensive work.
rule.description: Problem: With Reactor Flux.parallel.runOn, the data is divided on a number of 'rails' matching the number of CPU cores. This is only useful in case much CPU processing is performed: if the sequential form takes more than 0,1 ms of CPU time. With remote calls this is usually not the case. In addition, it introduces more complexity with risk of failures. Solution: Remove parallel().runOn. Unless the CPU work takes more than 0,1 ms in sequential form and proves to be faster with parallelization. So only for large collections and much CPU processing. (jpinpoint-rules)
